summary: CCC-built 1936-37 steel lookout on Flat Top Mountain; state-staffed until 1990; now amid an antenna farm by WinterPlace, with no public access documented.

facts.design: Steel tower with a glassed observation room at the top and a log cabin for the observer at the foot

Last regularly staffed fire tower in West Virginia

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The February 1936 notice says 80 feet; the December 1936 report gives steel for a 79-foot structure. Neither is confirmed as the finished height, so no height is recorded.
The Register lists Raleigh County; the 1936 reports place the knob on the Raleigh-Mercer boundary; the 2024 state entry says the Mercer/Raleigh county line.

notes_for_editor: History is well sourced from 1936-37 newspaper transcriptions on Forest Lookouts. Current access is not documented in any source read, so no access level is recorded. The 2024 records request was marked granted but its outcome is not on the page. The Wriston article PDF (firelookout.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/pop-wriston-built-the-big-ones.pdf) returned no text through fetch_text and may name the tower model; unverified. No photos added (licenses not stated). A local history column (ptonline.net) mentions a family that owned land up to the knob top, including a former lookout tower; its date and scope are unclear, so it is not used.
